note: v3363: HEART: absent_from asks whether a changed file reached the eye at all and answers by the presence of its diff --git header. Truncation cuts MID-FILE, so a file whose header arrived and whose body was chopped is absent-clean, blind_to-clean and unread, and every reach check built before this says it was seen. MEASURED with the shipped function over 16 versions: 67 files ARRIVED and 8 came in under half their bytes, headed by tv/second_eye_ledger.py on v3354 at 48.6 percent, the file that version exists to change, filed blind_to empty and verdict clean. v3361 repeated it at maximum volume: the answer OPENED with REACH 19 of 92 hunks naming the pre-push hook and the scoped walk, the entire version, as unjudgeable, and the row still read clean. The row now stores got and total PER FILE and the bar lives in the reader as REACH_CUT_BAR, so it can move without rewriting history. AND THE FIRST CUT WAS 71 percent NOISE, caught only by pointing it at his real history rather than at the fixture: it flagged 41 of 100 files with 33 at exactly zero, files that did not arrive SHORT but did not arrive at all and were already named in absent. That is the v3354 furniture defect re-created two versions after I fixed it, and a fixture built to show a half-cut file contains no wholly-cut file so it could never have caught it. One shared _file_sections now owns the diff-header boundary rule for both the ship-note strip and the measurement. Heart row eye reach per file registered in all five registries and it answers UNKNOWN rather than OK when no look has been recorded yet. ALSO FIXED A PRE-EXISTING RED OF MINE FROM v3359: WATCHES declared th-shelfov, a DOM element id, where organ_matrix.surfaces holds engine surfaces and zero of its 60 names is a DOM id, so it matched nothing for four versions while looking like coverage, invisible locally because the pre-push derives its gates from CHANGED TEST FILES. 4 red-proofs PROVEN, one of which was BLIND on its first attempt because the law counted only the double-quoted spelling of the walk.
